lines: Ding! That was for the cat on the wall. She nodded.
Biscuit! Hello! Ding ding, just for you!
Biscuit chased my front wheel for three whole metres. Hero.
A gull is racing me. He is winning. Obviously, he has wings.
Gull on the lamp post. Gull on the bench. Gull on my route!
I ring the bell at every corner. Corners love it.
Pedal, pedal, coast. Pedal, pedal, coast. Afternoon rhythm.
Sunflowers in the basket. They face forward. Good navigators.
New ribbon on the handlebars. Yellow. Very fast colour.
I oiled the chain this morning. Listen. Silence. Bliss.
One lap for errands, one lap for fun. This is the fun one.
Humming as I ride. The bike hums along. Mostly in tune.
The promenade is extra long today. In the best way.
Library book in the basket. Chapter nine at the next bench.
Ding! Sorry, gull. Lovely to see you, gull.
Shade, sun, shade, sun. Riding under the palms is a song.
My bell has a little dent. It makes it ring higher. Perfect.
Coasting past the fountain. It waves. I wave back.
A peach from the market, wobbling in the basket. Hold on!
The cat on the wall has not moved since Tuesday. Admirable.
String lights not on yet. I will ride by later and check.
Through the square, round the kiosk, one more hill. Wheee.
Straw hat on, wind in the brim. Very Riviera of me.
Biscuit sat for my bell. Yusuf is training him well.
Gulls on the railing in a row. Like a little choir.
That song from the café is stuck in my pedals now.
Slow lap today. The town deserves to be looked at.
Ding! Ding! That one was just because I am happy.
Basket inventory: one book, two pears, one sunbeam.
The cypresses lean the way I lean. Friends.
Bike polished, bell polished, me slightly polished.
Errands done. Now I am just riding. Best errand.
Left at the palm, right at the lemon tree. I could do it asleep.
A lavender sprig behind my ear. For aerodynamics.
Little bump by the kiosk. Whoop! Every time. Love it.
The cat on the wall blinked at me. That means hello.
My knitting is in the basket. The bike is wearing a scarf soon.
Second coffee, sunny chair, book open. Afternoon complete.
Crossword clue: fast, two wheels, five letters. Lucie!
Seven across, a small cake. Six letters. Madeleine? Obviously.
A gull is eyeing my croissant. Not today, monsieur.
Fine, gull. One crumb. Do not tell your friends.
Biscuit is under the next table. I can see one happy tail.
The cat on the wall is watching my milk. Very politely.
Marcel put on the accordion record. Toes tapping already.
Chapter twelve and a pain au chocolat. Good pairing.
The bike waits by the chair like a good dog.
Sugar cube, stir, sip, sigh. My afternoon ritual.
I am reading a novel about a baker. Research, obviously.
Postcards to write: four. Postcards written: one. Lovely pace.
Sketching the fountain on a napkin. It came out as a cake.
This chair gets the sun at exactly two. I plan my day around it.
Crossword nearly done. Henri will be so impressed.
Little almond biscuit with the coffee. Tiny joy, big joy.
Every afternoon, same chair, same coffee, new crumbs.
Someone is whistling the song from the radio. It is me.
I brought my own napkin with a bicycle on it. Matching!
Watching the string lights sway. They are practising for tonight.
Reading the same page twice because the view is better.
Coffee in one hand, book in the other, sun on both.
Gull on the umbrella. He likes the shade too.
My poetry book has a pressed flower in it. From this café.
Bell on the bike, spoon on the cup. Two little dings.
Learning a song on the ukulele. Three chords, all cheerful.
I take my coffee with a view and a little more sugar.
Planning tomorrow's ride on a napkin map. Lots of loops.
This is my sitting part of the day. I am very good at it.
The tarte au citron is looking at me. I am looking back.
Watching Léo do laps. He would make a fine cyclist.
Biscuit got a crust from Marcel. Biscuit is radiant.
Word game with myself: name every pastry. I am on nineteen.
The waiter hums, I hum, the café hums. Good acoustics.
A cushion on the chair today. Marcel spoils us.
Five minutes of sun on my face, then the crossword.
I knit one row per sip. This scarf is very caffeinated.
The radio is playing something with a trumpet. Yes.
Oh, the cat on the wall rolled over. Big afternoon for her.
Afternoons here smell like lemons and warm bread. Every one.
A gull landed on my basket. Passenger of the day!
Biscuit! Who is a good boy? Biscuit is. Obviously.
Three things I love: bells, books, and the four o'clock light.
Bike ride, then coffee, then bike ride. The perfect sandwich.
Henri is watering the lemon tree again. It is glowing.
Odile waved from the bench. I rang twice. Our code.
The fountain sounds like someone laughing quietly.
Is it too early for an ice cream? No. Never.
I have a library card and a bike. I am unstoppable.
Sun on the zinc roofs. Everything looks freshly ironed.
Camille and Théo strolling. They match today. Sweet.
My tyre pump is shaped like a little rocket. I adore it.
Gulls take afternoon naps on the railing. Wise birds.
Picked up a seashell. It lives in the bell basket now.
The whole town is on its second coffee. Including me.
A song from an open window. I slowed down to listen.
Bougainvillea over the wall, cat under it. A painting.
Afternoon plan: nothing urgent, everything lovely.
Marcel brought an extra sugar cube. He just knows.
Merci, Marcel! Best cup in town, and I have tried them all.
Sun on the table, sun in the cup. Two suns. Lucky me.
I saved the chair next to me for the breeze. It came!
Somebody left a daisy on my saucer. Whoever you are, thank you.
Coffee, croissant, a little nap with my eyes open.
The umbrella makes the nicest stripe of shade. Very chic.
I gave my last crumb to a sparrow. He said merci. I think.
This cup is warm, this chair is warm, I am warm. Bliss.
Two sips left. I am making them last all afternoon.
Your scarf is gorgeous, madame! The exact colour of apricots.
Marcel remembered I like the cup with the blue rim. Hero.
Stirring slowly. Afternoon coffee deserves slow stirring.
I passed the salt to the next table. We are friends now.
My helmet has its own chair. It works hard, it deserves one.
Writing a thank-you card for the baker. With a doodle of bread.
The breeze keeps flipping my napkin. Playful thing.
Watching the cups go by on Marcel's tray. Like a parade.
Saving half the croissant for later. Later is now. Oops.
The foam had a little leaf today. Marcel is an artist.
Honestly the best seat. You can see the fountain wink.
Thank you for the water, Marcel! With lemon, even. Spoiled.
Feet up on the bike pedal. Very elegant, I know.
The lady at table three lent me her pen. Such a nice pen.
Is that jasmine? Somebody's balcony is showing off.
My cup and the sky are the same blue today. I checked.
I tipped in buttons once. Marcel kept them. Sweet man.
Little spoon, little cup, big afternoon. Perfect.
Henri waved with his watering can. A very wet hello.
Sun on my knees. My knees say thank you.
I am resting my legs so they can show off later.
I told Marcel his apron is very dashing. He blushed!
One more minute. The breeze just got here, it would be rude.
Ding! Thank you for waving, madame! Ding again!
The breeze is pushing me uphill. Very helpful breeze.
Ding! Bonne après-midi, everyone! All of you!
A man held the gate for my bike. Très gallant!
Pedalling slowly so the afternoon lasts longer.
The cypresses are bowing in the wind. Merci, merci.
Peaches in the basket! A gift from the kiosk. Spoiled.
Ringing my bell for the fountain. It splashed back.
Coasting past the promenade. Hello, sea breeze. Hello, palms.
The bell sounds better in the afternoon. Warmer, somehow.
Odile complimented my basket. I may never recover.
Wind in my hair, sun on my arms, bread somewhere. Perfect.
Slowing down for Léo. He is a very important pedestrian.
I gave Henri a lemon from my basket. He gave me two back.
Lavender on the corner. I always brake for lavender.
The road is warm. The tyres purr. We are all very content.
Bonjour, little dog! Your ears are flying. So are mine.
The breeze smells of salt and fig leaves today.
Delivering a croissant to a friend. Express service.
Stopping to fix a lady's bag strap. Three seconds. Done!
Everyone on the promenade is smiling. I checked them all.
Bell, wave, ding, wave. My afternoon in four words.
The palms are clapping. Thank you, thank you, too kind.
Shade under the plane trees. Like riding through a hug.
A kid pointed at my basket and said wow. Same, kid.
Gentle hill, gentle breeze, gentle me. Ding.
Carrying flowers for the kiosk lady. She loves yellow ones.
Look, the shutters are all open. The houses are breathing.
Riding past the café so Marcel can wave. He always does.
My shadow is riding beside me. Very good company.
Ding for Camille! Ding for Théo! Dings for everybody!
The afternoon sun makes every wall look like butter.
What a breeze. Somebody ordered it just for us.
Thank you, sunshine. Same time tomorrow?
Late summer is the best summer. It stays a bit longer.
I smiled at a gull. The gull looked flattered.
Everyone looks so nice today. Truly, everyone.
The fig tree by the steps is dropping little presents.
My cheeks are pink from the sun. Very rosé of me.
Henri says the lemons are ahead of schedule. Bravo, lemons.
Warm stone, cool breeze, the whole town humming.
Someone painted their door mint green. I approve completely.
Afternoons are for little favours. I have done three.
The sun is generous today. I am trying to match it.
Bougainvillea everywhere. The walls are wearing pink.
Odile and Henri on the bench, shoulder to shoulder. Sweet.
I returned a lost glove to the kiosk. Glove is safe.
The fountain sounds extra cheerful in this heat.
I complimented a hat today. The hat deserved it.
Thank you to whoever planted the geraniums. Magnificent.
Every window box is in bloom. Showing off. Good.
I said bonjour so many times I lost count. Wonderful.
The sea is that sleepy afternoon blue. Very restful.
Léo just did a lap of the fountain backwards. Bravo, Léo!
The fountain is doing its little afternoon sparkle. Lovely.
Two kids, one fountain, a hundred laps. I am counting for them.
Somebody's kite is up over the promenade. A yellow one!
I came for one coffee. The afternoon had other plans.
Léo waved at me with both arms. I waved with both arms back.
Somebody laughed at the fountain and now everyone is smiling.
The bike is parked where I can see it. It is having a rest too.
This cup is so warm. I am holding it like a small kitten.
Marcel is polishing glasses for later. Rosé glasses. I noticed.
The pigeons are queueing for crumbs. Very orderly pigeons.
A spoon, a saucer, a tiny biscuit. The café thinks of everything.
Watching the fountain is basically a hobby. My best hobby.
Henri walked past twice. Same hat, same smile. Both lovely.
Merci, Marcel! Yes, the little almond one. Obviously.
Little feet splashing at the fountain edge. Pure happiness.
The shadows are getting long and lazy. Me too.
Somebody's grandmother just won a game of pétanque. Applause!
My coffee has a little heart and my heart has a little coffee.
I ordered nothing. Marcel brought it anyway. Exactly right.
Odile is feeding a sparrow from her hand. The sparrow is honoured.
Afternoon rule: no rushing. Second rule: also no rushing.
Léo told me the fountain is magic. I believe him completely.
I tipped my chair back one inch. That is my holiday for today.
One more sip and then the bike. Or two more sips.
A child just gave Marcel a drawing of a croissant. Masterpiece.
The tablecloth is warm from the sun. Like a sleepy cat.
Thank you, sun. Thank you, chair. Thank you, coffee.
The kids are racing leaves down the fountain. Go, little green!
I am not lazy. I am appreciating. Very different.
Every table has a little vase. Mine has a daisy. Hello, daisy.
Somebody just ordered a hot chocolate in this sun. A legend.
The string lights are still asleep. Not long now, lights.
Coffee, sunshine, and Léo explaining gulls. Perfect afternoon.
That little girl in the red hat is winning tag. Go, red hat!
I keep meaning to leave. The afternoon keeps saying stay.
Marcel hummed the whole time he poured. The coffee tastes hummed.
I feel very lucky in this chair. Specifically this chair.
The cypresses are swaying like they heard music. Me too.
There is chalk on the promenade. Somebody drew a sun. Two suns!
One sugar. Two sugars. It is the afternoon, who is counting?
The fountain splashed my shoe. A little hello, obviously.
Little bow to Marcel for the foam. He bowed back. Très élégant.
Ding! Hello, fountain children! Ding ding!
The kids asked for a bell concert. One lap, many dings.
Round the fountain, slowly, for the little ones to wave at.
Léo is racing me on foot. He is winning. I am letting him.
Past the kiosk, past the palms, past the happiest dog in town.
The windows are catching the sun. The whole street is winking.
A little boy saluted my bike. My bike saluted back. Ding!
Long shadows on the promenade. I am racing my own shadow.
Bonjour, Odile! Bonjour, bench! Bonjour, everybody!
The lemon trees smell so good I went round them twice.
I stopped for a parade of children holding hands. Very cute traffic.
A kid gave my bike a flower for the basket. Best tip ever.
Ring for joy, ring for hello, ring because it is Tuesday.
Down the little hill, legs out. Wheee. Very dignified.
Marcel is untangling the string lights. Getting ready. Exciting!
The fountain spray made a rainbow. I rode right past it!
The lamps are not lit yet. Plenty of afternoon left.
Home soon for a little nap. A nap before rosé. Obviously.
Three children, one ice cream each, all on the same bench. Sweet.
The church bell rang four. I rang mine back. A duet.
I like this hour. Everybody's slow and nobody minds.
Henri's watering can is bigger than his lemon tree. Adorable.
Hello, hopscotch! I do not hop on bikes. But I want to.
The kiosk awning is pink in this light. Matching my cheeks.
One loop more. My legs said yes before I asked.
The breeze smells of peaches and sea salt. Unreasonably lovely.
A tiny girl rode her tricycle beside me. Fastest tricycle ever.
Lap of honour for the fountain. It has been working very hard.
A soap bubble just floated past my handlebars. Hello, bubble!
Ding to the left, ding to the right. Everybody gets a ding.
Leaning into the corner like a professional. A small professional.
What a gift, an ordinary afternoon. Really.
Today I am grateful for: bells, foam, Léo, and peaches.
The town is quiet in the best way. Like a happy sigh.
I love when the light goes honey-coloured. It is going now.
Children at the fountain, gulls on the roofs. All present.
Some days you just say merci to everything. Today, obviously.
Peaches, a ribbon and a little cake. Nobody needs more.
Soon the lamps. Then the rosé. Then the dancing. Hooray.
Lucie's afternoon report: sunny, sweet, ninety percent bell.
I smiled at a stranger and now she is smiling at a stranger.
Léo says the fountain is singing. If you listen, it is.
I have nowhere to be until rosé. What a rich woman I am.
Bonjour, Léo! Faster than me today? Obviously not.
Hello, hello, hello! That was three people. Efficient.
The café smells of cinnamon from all the way up here.
Someone is frying onions. Somewhere. Wonderful someone.
Hear that? The fountain is gossiping again.
My chain goes tick tick tick. Happy bike noises.
Warm stones, sea salt, sun cream. Afternoon, bottled.
The gulls are laughing. At what? Who knows. Lovely.
I wonder who lives behind the blue shutters. Someone tidy.
Where is Léo off to with that bucket? Big plans, clearly.
Which way, left or right? Both. Obviously both.
Does the kiosk ever run out of peaches? I must ask.
Is that a new bench? It looks very sittable.
Is it tarte day at the café? It smells like tarte day.
Why do cypresses always look so pleased with themselves?
Bell, wheels, wind in my ears. My favourite song.
One more lap past the café. For the smell. Obviously.
Bread oven, still warm at three. The bakery never stops.
Someone is practising piano. Same three notes. Charming.
The zinc roofs are humming in the heat. Or is that me?
Bonjour, madame! Yes, the basket is new! Well, newish.
Hi, Théo! Did you find the good baguette? Of course you did.
Wave to the neighbour, wave to the cat, wave to the sea.
I wonder what the gulls talk about. Lunch, probably.
A slow lap. A sniffing-the-flowers lap.
Shutters clicking open after siesta. Click, click, hello.
Ding! Hello, open window! Yes, I wave at windows.
How many tiles in the promenade? Léo will know.
Is that orange blossom or the kiosk's marmalade? Both!
Bonjour, string lights. Not yet, I know. Soon.
Coffee smell on the left, sea smell on the right. Balance.
Hello, Henri's hat! Henri is under it, I assume.
Do you think the fountain gets dizzy? It never stops.
The kiosk is playing accordion again. I am riding in time.
Bonjour, bonjour! I say it twice so it lasts longer.
The basket smells of strawberries. Guess what is in it.
Ding! Hello, visitors! The café is that way! You will see.
Tyres on cobbles go brrrr. Tyres on paving go shhh.
I followed a butterfly for half a street. Worth it.
Where does the sea breeze go after the promenade? Up here!
The bakery window has a new cake. I am investigating.
Ding for Odile, ding for Henri, a double ding for the bench.
Afternoon, everyone! I mean everyone. Even the palms.
Wait, is that a lemon on the path? Henri! A runaway!
Bonjour, Marcel! The usual, plus a surprise.
Marcel, is that cardamom I smell? You are a genius.
Listen. Cups, spoons, a little laugh. Café music.
Is the lemon tart new, or have I just never noticed?
Cocoa on top, cinnamon underneath. Marcel has layers.
Do you think Marcel dreams in coffee? I do.
Afternoon, Henri! Join me? There is a chair and a biscuit.
The milk steamer just sang. Bravo, milk steamer.
I wonder what Odile is reading. She smiles at every page.
Fresh madeleines. I can hear them being warm.
Hello, Léo! Yes, that is whipped cream. Yes, it is mine.
Marcel, what is the cake of the day? Ah. Obviously yes.
The awning flaps like it is clapping for my coffee.
Sugar cube in, tiny splash. Best sound of the afternoon.
Somebody ordered a crêpe. The whole terrace knows.
Is Camille having the tarte or the éclair? Watching closely.
Bonjour, Théo! You look like a man who just had a nap.
Orange peel and espresso. Who knew? Marcel knew.
Salut, Camille! Your hat matches the awning. Gorgeous.
Chairs scraping, a dog yawning. Very busy, very calm.
What makes the foam so tall today? Happiness, he says.
One almond croissant to share. With myself. Later.
The fountain is just loud enough to sound like applause.
Hello to the next table. Their cake looks very cheerful.
Why does coffee taste better outside? Big question. Sip.
Afternoon smells: warm bread, cut grass, a little sunscreen.
Bonjour! Have you tried the kiosk peaches? Do. Obviously.
Listen. Somebody is laughing on a balcony. Lovely.
Hello, cypress. You have grown a whole centimetre.
I wonder if the sea ever gets bored of being blue. No.
Afternoon, neighbour! Your tomatoes are showing off.
Is it me, or does the town smell of apricots today?
Hello, hello! Afternoons are for saying hello a lot.
The breeze brought the café to me. Very thoughtful breeze.
Practising my track stand. Two seconds! Then a wobble. Progress.
Left turn, little twirl. Signalling with style.
I am learning every street by its smell. This one is basil.
Practising a slow, graceful stop. Like a swan. A swan on wheels.
I learned to ride on this promenade. Papa ran behind me, laughing.
My first bike had a white basket. This one is its grandchild.
That was a swift. I think. Bird names are my new hobby.
Practising my bell in waltz time. Ding, ding-ding. Ding, ding-ding.
Fixed my own puncture last week. Henri clapped. I bowed.
Right here is where I first saw the string lights. I gasped.
New skill: carrying a cake on a bike. So far, one perfect cake.
I am teaching myself the names of the hills. This one is mine now.
Whistling while pedalling. Breathing is the tricky bit.
Counting pedal strokes to the café. Today: two hundred and six.
My first summer here, I got lost on purpose every day. Still do.
Practising hello in Norwegian. Hei! Hei hei! Very bouncy word.
I am learning to read the wind from the palm tops. Easterly. Nice.
I once rode this lane with a bunch of balloons. Floated a bit.
Gear three is my friend. Gear five and I are still chatting.
Practising for the town bike parade. My bell is ready. Am I?
The year it snowed, I pushed the bike here. Snowman by the kiosk!
Packing the basket is a puzzle. Pears go on top.
I am practising a very small bunny hop. Bunny is optimistic.
My aunt taught me to ride slow on hills. Steady, steady, view.
Learning the shortcut behind the lemon trees. Shh. Secret.
I practise my bonjour voice uphill. It gets more musical.
This is the hill where I won a race against a pigeon. Long ago.
Lesson from Théo: ride past the bakery twice. Smell, then decide.
I painted the bell myself one rainy week. Little blue stars.
A figure eight round two planters. Nearly round!
Learning which cobbles wobble. That one. And that one. Hello!
First day with the new saddle. We are getting to know each other.
I learned to ride in a skirt here. Clip on the hem. Genius.
Practising my left-hand wave. The right hand was getting famous.
The first time Henri waved at me, I nearly rode into a hedge.
My bicycle drawings always get two different wheels. Charming.
Loopy L on every postcard. Very proud of that L.
Marcel is teaching me to taste coffee. Notes of... sunshine?
Practising the café song on my knee. Drum, drum, sip.
This table is where I met my best friend. She stole my sugar.
My first coffee alone, aged sixteen. Right here. Felt so grown up.
Watercolour today. My fountain is mostly a puddle. Lovely puddle.
Practising tonight's dance steps under the table. Shh.
Memorising a little poem for Odile's birthday. Stanza two!
I am learning to say no to a second croissant. Lesson postponed.
Marcel showed me how he folds napkins. Mine looks like a hat.
Remember when the whole terrace sang for Marcel's birthday? Joy.
Learning to read slower. Good books deserve the long afternoon.
French knots on my embroidery. Each one a tiny bun.
I learned to make foam at home. It is more of a cloud. A happy one.
This chair! Where I read my first whole book in one sitting.
A spoon balanced on my nose! Two seconds. Marcel says keep going.
Practising the accordion fingering on the tablecloth. Silent music.
The day the café got its new awning, we all toasted with lemonade.
Learning the names of Marcel's cups. This one is called Bertrand.
I am practising patience. The tarte comes out at four. Patience.
Copying Odile's recipe for madeleines into my little book.
Learning to sketch faces. Marcel says I gave him lovely eyebrows.
Practising a new laugh. No, I am joking. Same laugh, more often.
The first time Marcel drew a heart in my foam, I took a photo.
I folded a paper crane. It is a paper duck. Cute.
Revising my bike map with new favourite corners. Six this week.
My first ever crossword finished, right at this table. Framed it.
Learning a card trick for Léo. Pick a card. Any card. Not that one.
I practise my good posture here. Then the croissant arrives.
Learning to tell the time by the shadow of the umbrella. Ten past?
Practising writing with my left hand. It looks like a gull wrote it.
This is where Henri taught me chess. I still open with my horse.
Learning to make the perfect lemonade. Step one: Henri's lemons.
Practising pronunciation: pain au chocolat. Perfect. Obviously.
I learned to whistle with two fingers here. Very loud. Very useful.
Doodling the cypresses. Practice makes taller cypresses.
Learning a new song for the dancing tonight. The chorus is easy!
I learned to swim on the beach below. Fearless. Mostly fearless.
Juggling three lemons. Two lemons. Okay, one lemon.
The first day I came here, Marcel gave me a free pastry. Welcome!
I keep a notebook of nice things people say. Page forty today.
Practising my thank-you face. It is just my normal face. Good.
Remember the kite festival? My kite was a croissant. It flew!
Hello, hibiscus! I am naming every flower in town.
This is where I did my first ever pirouette. On grass. Graceful.
Learning the town's history. The fountain is older than Henri!
I once found a four-leaf clover by the steps. Still in my wallet.
Learning to tie a ribbon bow one-handed. Life skill.
Practising standing still for a whole minute. Lovely minute.
Every afternoon I learn one new neighbour's name. Today: Paulette.
Learning the dance from last night. Step, step, spin, giggle.
The bougainvillea goes purple at this hour. Very dramatic of it.
Henri's lemon tree is glowing. Or that is the string lights. Both!
Tomorrow: bakery, then the flower stall. In that order. Obviously.
My grandmother leaned on railings exactly like this. Elbows first.
Jasmine just opened. I can smell it from here. Hello, jasmine.
Plan for tomorrow: geraniums in the basket. Red ones. Lots.
The sky is the colour of plum jam. I will have some at breakfast.
Mamie said blue hour is when flowers tell secrets. I am listening.
One more minute here. Then dancing. Then bed. A perfect itinerary.
The cypresses look like they are wearing their evening coats.
Ding. That was for the first star. It gets a bell.
Someone's window box has pansies. Tiny faces, all saying bonsoir.
Note to self: ask Henri how he gets lemons that shiny.
My brother and I raced bikes on a promenade like this. I won. Mostly.
The palms are just silhouettes now. Very elegant silhouettes.
Tomorrow I am buying lavender. A whole bunch. For the bike.
Blue sky, warm railing, rosé still in my cheeks. Lovely.
That bougainvillea has climbed one more balcony. Bravo, you.
I promised Maman a postcard of this. It will have to try very hard.
The lamps come on one, two, three. Like a little parade.
Second-best view in town. The best is this one, tomorrow.
Fig tree by the steps is heavy with figs. Breakfast plan: figs.
Papa always said: lean, breathe, look up. I am doing all three.
I can see my balcony from here. The basil is waving.
Blue hour. My favourite colour, my favourite hour. Obviously.
Tomorrow the market has peaches. I have already decided on six.
The oleander smells like sugar tonight. Sweet thing.
Little plan: watch the sky, then the lights, then the stars.
When I was small I thought the sky did this just for me. It does.
The lemon trees on the terrace look like they are holding lanterns.
Somebody planted marigolds by the fountain. I approve. Strongly.
I will cycle up to the church tomorrow. For the roses. And the hill.
The hibiscus closed for the night. Good night, hibiscus.
The rosemary by the kiosk smells like Sunday lunch at Mamie's.
Blue on blue on blue. Then one pink cloud. Show-off.
Tomorrow I am oiling the bell. It deserves a spa day.
Grandpapa grew tomatoes on his balcony. Enormous ones. Champions.
I want a lemon tree. A small one. For the window. Tomorrow, maybe.
The geraniums on the zinc roofs look like they were painted on.
Elbows on the rail, chin on hands. Professional sky watcher.
The bougainvillea and the sky are having a purple competition.
My sister calls at nine on Sundays. I will tell her about this.
The string lights are on. The whole promenade just smiled.
Mamie pressed flowers in her cookbook. I found a violet once.
Tomorrow's croissant is already promised to me. I asked nicely.
Sea air and orange blossom. The town should bottle it.
I counted three lit windows with plants in them. Cosy, cosy, cosy.
The sky is doing that blue that looks like velvet. Ooh.
Next week I am painting my shutters. Lemon yellow. Obviously.
Papa taught me to ride on a street just like this one.
Somebody is watering a window box up there. Same idea as Henri.
Plan for Saturday: picnic by the cypresses. Bring cherries.
